messages:
emily: Quick heads-up — noticed embed endpoint example in API ref (rust snippet) shows "Vec<&str>" body but our handler expects [{"id":...,"text":...}]. This causes SDK users to get 400s. Anyone else seen reports? :eyes:

sam: Oof, saw a customer bug about this earlier. Can you paste the snippet?

emily: Sure — from docs currently:
```rust
let resp = client.post("/v1/embeddings")
  .json(&json!({"input": ["a string", "another"]}))
  .send().await?;
```
But the server expects:
```json
{"input": [{"id": "1", "text": "a string"}, {"id":"2", "text":"another"}]}
```

jordan: Confirmed — runtime will accept either simplified strings for backward compat, but our openapi schema and rust example must match the object form when using batch metadata. If example suggests simple array it misleads folks who need ids.

rachel: Can someone open a docs PR to replace the example and add a short migration note? Also link to the embeddings schema file so we don't forget to update OpenAPI samples.

emily: I've opened a draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/2098 — replaces rust snippet and updates the example JSON. Needs a quick review.

sam: I'll review. Small nit: in the rust snippet use serde_json::json! and show types — e.g.,
```rust
let body = json!({"input": [{"id":"1","text":"hi"}]});
let resp = client.post("/v1/embeddings").json(&body).send().await?;
```
That reduces confusion.

rachel: Also add a one-line migration guide in the top of the embeddings doc: "If you previously passed an array of strings, wrap each string in an object with key 'text' and optional 'id'."

emily: Good call, will add. I'll also add a cross-link to the SDK snippets page so other languages get mirroring.

docs-bot: deploy-preview created for PR #2098 — https://deploy-preview-2098--docs.redwood.ai :white_check_mark:

sam: Reviewed and approved. :thumbsup:

emily: thanks all — merging after one more test run.
